title: Help for carers
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: TOM: And be ready to tell them about anything you find particularly difficult about caring for your mother.

CAROL: So recently I’ve noticed she’s started to have quite bad problems with her memory … if I wasn’t there, I think she’d forget to eat, for example. And often she doesn’t seem quite sure what day it is.
TOM: Yes, tell them about that. And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her? Lifting her, for example?
CAROL: Yes. She’s quite heavy, and I’m afraid of hurting my back – I’d be in real trouble if that happened.
TOM: They can give you advice about that, and also about how to avoid the possibility of your mum having a fall.
CAROL: Great. So once they’ve done this assessment, if I’m eligible, what happens next?
TOM: Well, they might support you financially. So they might help you with transport costs, like if you have to get a taxi to take your mother for an appointment, for example.
CAROL: I usually drive her myself actually. So could I claim for the petrol?
TOM: You could, and you can claim for the insurance too.

TOM: And if you need help with the housework, they can arrange for someone to come along once or twice a week. And one other thing, I hope you don’t mind me saying this, but it’s important you look after yourself, and it seems to me you’re under quite a bit of stress.
TOM: Well, tell the council, because they may be able to give you some advice on how to minimise it.
CAROL: Really? Though actually I feel so much better having talked to you. I’ll get in touch with the council straight away. Now shall we …

3. 根据列点结构以及短横线并列结构，可知本题填入护工需做的一项具体事务，上一行的关键词dressing在原文里替换为getting dressed。并列词and also后出现答案shower。

4. 和本题并列的helping with meals在原文中替换为help her at mealtimes。下一句并列连词and后引出答案money。deal with替换为cope。

6. 根据题干的宾语her可知需要填入动词，而和下一题题干的preventing比对可知，很可能填入动名词形式。上一题谈论memory结束后，男士问“And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her?”，提示本题即将出现。并且下一句男士就以询问的形式说出了答案lifting，随后女士给了肯定的回答。考生需要提前做好词性预判，并在男士提出询问时就留意答案。

7. 原文讨论lifting her之后通过and also引出下一题，preventing替换为avoid，随后出现答案fall。

8. 题干中的transport costs原词重现，e.g.替换为like，随后出现答案taxi。

9. 题干中的fuel替换为petrol，下一句男士在回答后，通过并列连词and引出和fuel并列的insurance。

10. 题干上一行的housework原词重现，And one other thing提示并列结构。下一句由男士说出答案stress，而在后续进一步说明中才出现题干中reduce的同义替换词minimise。考生需要在听到housework后就注意并列关联词，并且留意能够和reduce搭配的名词。

Local councils can arrange practical support to help those caring for elderly people at home.

This can give the carer:
• time for other responsibilities
• a [1] ______

Assessment of mother’s needs
This may include discussion of:
• how much [2] ______the caring involves
• what types of tasks are involved, e.g.
   - help with dressing
   - helping her have a [3] ______
   - shopping
   - helping with meals
   - dealing with [4] ______
• any aspects of caring that are especially difficult, e.g.
   - loss of [5] ______
   - [6] ______her
   - preventing a [7] ______

Types of support that may be offered to carers
• transport costs, e.g. cost of a [8] ______
• car-related costs, e.g. fuel and [9] ______
• help with housework
• help to reduce [10] ______

transcriptHtml:
TOM: And be ready to tell them about anything you find particularly difficult about caring for your mother.
CAROL: So recently I’ve noticed she’s started to have quite bad problems with her memory … if I wasn’t there, I think she’d forget to eat, for example. And often she doesn’t seem quite sure what day it is.
TOM: Yes, tell them about that. And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her? Lifting her, for example?
CAROL: Yes. She’s quite heavy, and I’m afraid of hurting my back – I’d be in real trouble if that happened.
TOM: They can give you advice about that, and also about how to avoid the possibility of your mum having a fall.
CAROL: Great. So once they’ve done this assessment, if I’m eligible, what happens next?
TOM: Well, they might support you financially. So they might help you with transport costs, like if you have to get a taxi to take your mother for an appointment, for example.
CAROL: I usually drive her myself actually. So could I claim for the petrol?
TOM: You could, and you can claim for the insurance too.
CAROL: Oh, right.
TOM: And if you need help with the housework, they can arrange for someone to come along once or twice a week. And one other thing, I hope you don’t mind me saying this, but it’s important you look after yourself, and it seems to me you’re under quite a bit of stress.
CAROL: I am, yes.
TOM: Well, tell the council, because they may be able to give you some advice on how to minimise it.
CAROL: Really? Though actually I feel so much better having talked to you. I’ll get in touch with the council straight away. Now shall we …
